variants.headline: Looking back: money in hand, no food to buy
variants.sub: People have money for food but cannot buy it because shops and farms are sold out.
variants.body:
We return to our earlier coverage. Our report recorded this: Shops and farms were sold out of food, leaving people with money unable to buy meals.

Our principles must be able to describe a material need accurately. Purchasing power is not a meal when food cannot be obtained. A political argument that loses the distinction has lost the practical problem, however warmly it speaks about the people whose money cannot secure what they need.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We hold {target} to account critically. People who can pay should not be left without food because provision fails, and a shortage of supply deserves more than an argument directed at the wrong problem.
